decisionSummary: Records the human/business decision after reviewing the Batch 4 approval packet. The two optics are standalone customer BoQ / pricing / export lines, NOT configuration-expansion children, and must not be auto-attached under any switch. The 11 historical-to-current replacement candidates remain deferred with no silent runtime SKU substitution. This record is NOT an approved Batch 4 runtime expansion rule pack and creates none; the configuration-expansion composer/selector remains Batch 1 + Batch 2 + Batch 3 only.
businessDecision: Optics appeared in the Batch 4 review because the Honeywell input BoQ listed them as standalone customer-requested SKUs, not because they are children of a switch. In the CCW exercise they were validated separately: SFP-10G-LR-S= is a standalone 10GBASE-LR SFP module at quantity 12, and SFP-10/25G-LR-S= is a standalone 10/25GBASE-LR SFP28 module at quantity 14. They therefore belong in the Honeywell scope as customer BoQ lines and pricing/export lines, but they must not be automatically attached under C9300X-48HX-A or C9300L-24P-4X-A unless a real design/evidence rule says which port or uplink consumes which optic. That is why optics stay out of the approved configuration-expansion batches: they are valid SKUs to price if the customer provides them, but they are not approved expansion children to invent or auto-add. The 11 historical-to-current replacement candidates remain deferred and no silent runtime SKU substitution is approved.
authoritySeparation: Configuration-expansion authority (which children to auto-add/default/offer under a parent) is separate from pricing/catalog authority (what a line costs). This record carries configuration-scope decisions only and encodes no price values. Any optic that is present in the accepted customer Honeywell scope is priced and exported from deterministic catalog/pricing inputs at runtime, never from this record and never by a runtime AI decision.
